claims.claim: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs withdrew a 28 September directive on asylum-application intake after violent protests in Durban and Soweto.
claims.episode_span: withdrew a directive on the intake of asylum applications after violent anti-immigration protests in Durban and Soweto
claims.source_title: South Africa: Home Affairs Withdraws Asylum Directive After Violent Anti-Immigration Protests
claims.supporting_quote: The Department of Home Affairs (DHA) has withdrawn a directive on the intake of asylum applications following violent anti-immigration protests in Durban and Soweto

claims.claim: The directive followed a July Constitutional Court judgment in the Scalabrini Centre of Cape Town case that struck down Refugees Act provisions blocking some asylum applications on procedural grounds.
claims.episode_span: followed a July Constitutional Court judgment in the Scalabrini Centre of Cape Town case
claims.source_title: South Africa: Home Affairs Withdraws Asylum Directive After Violent Anti-Immigration Protests
claims.supporting_quote: The directive, issued on 28 September, followed a July judgment by the Constitutional Court in the Scalabrini Centre of Cape Town case.

claims.claim: The judgment allows asylum applications regardless of how people entered and does not automatically grant refugee status or permanent residence.
claims.episode_span: lets people apply for protection regardless of how they entered South Africa, but it does not automatically grant refugee status or permanent residence
claims.source_title: South Africa: Home Affairs Withdraws Asylum Directive After Violent Anti-Immigration Protests
claims.supporting_quote: The judgment allows asylum seekers to apply for protection regardless of how they entered South Africa. However, it does not automatically grant applicants refugee status or permanent residence

claims.claim: Home Affairs said the director-general issued the directive without the minister's knowledge and that reception offices were overwhelmed.
claims.episode_span: the director-general issued the directive without the knowledge of the minister or other political office-bearers
claims.source_title: South Africa: Home Affairs Withdraws Asylum Directive After Violent Anti-Immigration Protests
claims.supporting_quote: Home Affairs said the directive was introduced as an operational measure to implement the court order but was issued by the department’s director-general without the knowledge of the minister or other political office-bearers.

claims.claim: Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi welcomed the withdrawal as relief that allows further consultation.
claims.episode_span: Panyaza Lesufi welcomed the withdrawal as a relief that opens room for further consultation
claims.source_title: South Africa: Home Affairs Withdraws Asylum Directive After Violent Anti-Immigration Protests
claims.supporting_quote: Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi has welcomed the department's decision, describing it as a relief that creates an opportunity for further consultation.
